summary: A high-priority arbitration ID (0x002) flooded the CAN bus at over 10 times its normal transmission rate, driving total bus load up by 62%. While the flood dominated the traffic volume, other baseline IDs continued transmitting at their expected rates, and no unknown IDs were observed. The detector registered maximum rate inflation and elevated bus load.

claims.text: The alert spans 4 seconds and contains 10423 frames from 50 arbitration IDs.
Average bus load reached 2606 msg/s, a 1.62x increase over the 1609 msg/s baseline.
ID 0x002 transmitted 4367 frames at 1091.75 msg/s, which is 10.95x its 99.68 msg/s baseline.
Other monitored baseline IDs (0x141, 0x140, 0x148, 0x25C) operated at approximately 1.0x their baseline rates.
No frames from IDs absent from the baseline were detected during the alert.
The vehicle function associated with ID 0x002 is unknown.

summary: The alert exhibits a classic fuzzing signature, characterized by the sudden appearance of 1,709 previously unseen arbitration IDs carrying high-entropy, random-looking payloads. Concurrently, legitimate traffic is severely suppressed, with overall bus load dropping to 12% of the baseline and many expected IDs going completely silent. This pattern indicates an active probing or fuzzing attack on the CAN bus rather than a benign state change.

claims.text: The alert spans 93.5 seconds and contains 17,437 frames from 1,759 arbitration IDs, of which 1,709 are absent from the baseline.
These unknown IDs carry payloads with high entropy (5.3–5.7 bits) and are transmitted at very low rates (~0.07–0.1 msg/s).
Overall bus load drops to 186 msg/s, which is only 12% of the 1,609 msg/s baseline.
Many baseline IDs are missing or running below 70% of their expected rate, including complete silences for IDs like 0x080, 0x150, and 0x160.
The detector scores highlight unknown_ids (1.0), missing_ids (1.0), and payload_entropy (0.93) as the primary anomalies.
